frequency_question: How often do observable precursor signals (tech transfer agreements, joint-venture announcements, facility preparation) in this signal state successfully culminate in operational domestic production within a short horizon?
membership_rule: Includes: documented state-level initiatives to localize production of advanced foreign missiles (e.g., air-to-ground or cruise missiles). Excludes: basic small arms, unguided munitions, or domestic designs built from scratch without foreign tech transfer.

cases.name: Ukraine Neptune missile domestic serial production ramp-up
Taiwan Hsiung Feng III production scaling with foreign-sourced subsystems
South Korea Taurus KEPD 350 integration and co-production discussions/agreements
Ukraine Vilkha-M rocket localization from Soviet baselines

coverage_note: 5 named cases representing advanced missile localization efforts; general historical base rate for high-urgency military tech localization when initial signals are visible is roughly 70-80%.
known_gaps: Extremely high-end Western cruise missiles like Storm Shadow have proprietary stealth and guidance tech that strictly limit rapid tech transfer compared to simpler rocket artillery.
skeleton: 5 historical proxy programs examined for rapid tech transfer and localized assembly under wartime or urgent acquisition pressure
multiplier: 4 hits out of 5 comparable advanced missile localization/co-production precursor tracks achieving operational status
validity_reason: Defense industrial base localization speeds and alliance technology-sharing frameworks remain stable over multi-year periods.
